answer: A random-walk trust graph makes fake identities expensive to hide. Every agent starts near a trusted seed, and short random walks spread trust through real social edges; a fresh account's ember glows faintly until walks from many seeds reach it, while a violet cluster of Sybils hangs off a few thin attack edges and stays dim. Forging one more identity means buying another genuine edge into the honest region, so cost grows with each fake, and copper-level walk-mass thresholds prune accounts below the line. Limits: slow-mixing graphs and bought edges weaken it, so seeds rotate and weights decay.
